Repository fengie/mhw-mods. Reuse the EXISTING branch feature/branch-lifecycle-enforcement-20260929 and EXISTING draft PR #196. Do not create any branch or PR.

The user explicitly wants force-enforced repository rules:
A) Agents must check branches first and reuse compatible branches instead of opening new branches.
B) Finished branches must be automatically and forcefully cleaned up.
C) Agent Control must enforce this mechanically, not only in documentation.

Current branch already contains an initial GLOBAL_GIT_DIRECTIVE.md rule requiring branch inventory/reuse. Build the full implementation on top of it.

Required implementation:

1. AGENTS.md + GLOBAL_GIT_DIRECTIVE.md
- Mandatory pre-branch inventory: git fetch --prune, local/remote branches, open PRs, live Agent Control tasks/leases.
- Reuse compatible unowned branch before creating a new one.
- Forbid retry/successor duplicate branches for same mutable scope unless existing branch is unsafe/incompatible and reason is recorded.
- One active implementation branch per mutable scope/lease.
- Branch cleanup is part of DONE; no task fully complete until cleanup succeeds.

2. Replace one-shot cleanup with permanent .github/workflows/branch-lifecycle-enforcer.yml
- retire/remove one-shot-superseded-branch-cleanup.yml.
- triggers: PR closed, push to main, workflow_dispatch, schedule hourly.
- self-hosted Windows mhw-mods runner is acceptable/preferred because hosted allocation can be unreliable.
- contents:write and pull-requests:read.
- preserve main, heaven-bridge, protected branches, and branches with open PRs.
- delete only with strong proof: branch tip ancestor of main OR exact current branch tip is a merged PR head to main and its merge commit is reachable from main OR explicit SHA-pinned superseded approval.
- race guard: ref tip must not move during audit.
- verify ref is gone after delete.
- preserve unique/unproven work, but surface it clearly in summary.
- fail the workflow if a proven-safe branch cannot be deleted.
- active PR protects implementation branch.
- add a repository-setting check for delete_branch_on_merge=true. If authenticated gh api/PATCH is available locally, make an idempotent setter script/workflow step; if not, fail/report exact remediation without secrets. Do not rely on paid rulesets.

3. Agent Control branch reuse
- tools/agent-control/server.mjs currently always creates agent/control-* branch. Change this.
- Before branch creation: fetch/prune, inventory local/remote branches.
- Exclude main/heaven-bridge, protected/reserved names, current branches owned by a live task/lease.
- Prefer reuse only on STRONG deterministic task/scope match. No fuzzy guessing. Explicit caller-provided base remains authoritative.
- Strong match can be based on normalized boundary/lane/task tokens and existing branch ownership metadata. If uncertain, create a new branch.
- Record decision evidence in task record: branchDecision ('reused'|'created'), candidate/rejection reasons, selected branch.
- Reused branch worktree must use existing ref without -b.
- A branch must be exclusively leased; prevent concurrent reuse by two agents.
- Add/extend API/CLI status so branches command or task view exposes the decision.

4. Completion cleanup enforcement in Agent Control
- A managed task is not fully complete while its controller-owned temporary branch still needs cleanup.
- When integration is VERIFIED on origin/main, safely remove worktree, local branch, and remote branch if it exists; verify deletion.
- Never delete unique/unmerged work.
- On cleanup failure, task => cleanup-required/blocked with nextAction; not done.
- Preserve failed/prelaunch branches for evidence, as existing behavior requires.
- Add tests for cleanup gating.

5. Tests
- Add unit/integration tests in tools/agent-control/test for:
  * eligible branch reused
  * live/leased branch rejected
  * no strong match => one new branch
  * concurrent duplicate branch ownership prevented
  * integrated branch cleanup succeeds
  * unique branch is preserved
  * cleanup failure prevents completion
- npm run check
- npm test
- structurally validate workflow YAML
- inspect git diff.
- Commit and push ONLY feature/branch-lifecycle-enforcement-20260929.
- Do NOT merge main. Report commit SHA, changed files, exact tests and any limitation.
